title: Chokepoints
hook: A handful of narrow straits carry the world's oil and goods.
notes: Oil flows from the US Energy Information Administration (World Oil Transit Chokepoints; Hormuz ≈ 20 million barrels/day in 2024, Malacca ≈ 23 million in 2023). Trade share and Red Sea disruption: UNCTAD, 2024. Routes are schematic; distances are computed along the drawn line.

scenes.title: Seven narrow doors
scenes.text: Most of the world's seaborne trade squeezes through a few straits and canals. Block one, and prices move worldwide within days.

scenes.title: Strait of Hormuz
scenes.text: About 20 million barrels of oil pass here every day, roughly a fifth of global consumption. At its narrowest the strait is about 33 km wide.

scenes.title: Strait of Malacca
scenes.text: The busiest oil route by volume, linking the Indian Ocean to China, Japan and Korea. Tens of thousands of ships a year thread between Malaysia and Sumatra.

scenes.title: The Red Sea detour
scenes.text: Since attacks on shipping began in late 2023, many ships avoid Suez and sail around Africa. Compare the two routes from Shanghai to Rotterdam.

scenes.title: The Panama Canal
scenes.text: The canal runs on fresh water from lakes. A severe drought in 2023 forced it to cut daily ship crossings by roughly a third, showing that climate is a chokepoint too.
